answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by pricing identity in time, not in names. A new identity begins as a nebula of unproven claims: it can only earn trust by completing small, verifiable jobs that established peers co-sign, each one adding a thin layer of quartz-hard reputation that cannot be bought or copied. Trust also decays, so a dormant knoll of old attestations slowly erodes unless the identity keeps doing honest work. One proven lie slashes the bond and voids the whole history. Spawning a thousand empty names is cheap; faking a thousand independent, time-tested work histories is not.
